yakone_goes_on_trial_over_international_.title: Yakone goes on trial over International Port bombing that killed 23, including a city councilor
yakone_goes_on_trial_over_international_.html:
Yakone, a Harbor Ward shipping broker, went on trial at the Republic City Circuit Court on Monday, charged with conspiracy and 23 counts of murder over the 14 May bombing at the International Port.

Deputy District Attorney Lian Okoro told the jury that Yakone arranged the delivery of the device to Pier Nine and the payments that funded it. He pleaded not guilty.

What happened

The explosion tore through a bonded warehouse on Pier Nine at 6:40 p.m., as dock crews were changing shifts. The Harbor Authority and Republic City General Hospital each put the dead at 23, including Councilor Shen Yiran of the Harbor Ward, who was at the pier to inspect a customs delay. Another 61 people were injured.

Police recovered a leaflet from the debris carrying a Salvationist slogan. No group has claimed responsibility.

The prosecution’s case

Okoro told the court that the device used a timer of Qianchan manufacture, and that a Qianchan trading house, Zhao-Meng and Sons, wired $140,000 to Yakone’s brokerage in the six weeks before the blast. He said the money was passed on to “persons who call themselves Salvationists.”

Okoro did not say what Qianchan would gain. He told the jury the state would show “who paid, not why.”

The Qianchan consulate told the Daily on Friday that it “has no knowledge of the firm’s accounts and rejects any suggestion of state involvement.” Zhao-Meng and Sons did not respond to requests for comment.

The defense

Yakone’s counsel, Marguerite Daw, told the jury the leaflet was printed on cheap paper available in any ward and that the Salvationist name was “put on this case in the first hour, and no one has asked since who wanted it there.” She said the transfers were routine payments for cargo insurance.

Councilor Shen was a vocal critic of the port’s brokerage fees. Daw said her client had lost business because of her and had no reason to kill her.

What’s next

Judge Rafael Imura said the trial is expected to run three weeks. The jury was seated on Friday after two days of questioning.

yakone_trial_everything_you_need_to_know.title: Yakone trial: Everything you need to know
yakone_trial_everything_you_need_to_know.html:
The trial of Yakone, the Harbor Ward shipping broker charged with conspiracy and 23 counts of murder over the 14 May bombing at the International Port, is expected to go to the jury this week.

Timeline

14 May 126 AG: A bomb destroys a bonded warehouse on Pier Nine, killing 23 people, including Councilor Shen Yiran, and injuring 61.

2 June: Yakone is arrested at his brokerage office.

21 June: A grand jury indicts him on all counts.

8 September: Trial opens before Judge Rafael Imura.

26 September: Ren Kaito, a former courier for Salvationist remnants, testifies for the prosecution under a plea agreement.

3 October: The court recesses for ten weeks after the Qianchan consulate contests a subpoena for the records of Zhao-Meng and Sons.

12 January 127 AG: Hearings resume.

28 January: The defense rests after Yakone testifies for two days. The charges. Conspiracy and 23 counts of murder. The maximum sentence is life imprisonment, since the United Republic has no death penalty.

The prosecution’s case. Deputy District Attorney Lian Okoro called 41 witnesses. The state says Yakone arranged the delivery of the device, and that $140,000 from Zhao-Meng and Sons passed through his brokerage to Salvationist remnants.

The defense’s case. Counsel Marguerite Daw called nine witnesses and says the leaflet found at the scene proves nothing, that the transfers were cargo insurance, and that Ren lied to earn his deal.

What is not in dispute. The blast, the 23 dead, and that the money moved. What it was for is the case.

The Daily draws on court filings and public hearings. Mr. Yakone’s counsel and the Qianchan consulate were offered a chance to comment on this explainer; neither replied.
